messages.author: e84e7628b5f8a3e1
messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] App darkens when using larger datatables
parts:
Jason,

I'm looking at your application. I can confirm that at least when I select "Baba, Hideo" your application is crashing because of out of memory conditions. I would look at reducing your memory footprint, perhaps by paginating your results.

-Andy

On Tue, Nov 17, 2015 at 1:02 AM, FreshMD <jason.m....@gmail.com> wrote:
Asked to start a new thread from my reply in this thread since the issues were just different enough to matter. (It was just going to be a quick 'me too' reply that got away from me... but I digress.)

My app grabs publication data from our university's Pure database so that our PIs can compare the publications there with data they have in the university library (called Tsubaki). The Pure part of my app (tab 1) is being cranky so we can forget the Tsubaki part (tabs 2 & 3) for now.

The problem comes when loading researchers with larger numbers of publications, however I have noticed that at least one researcher with 442 pubs (Akiyama, Hidenore) seems to load without problem but another researcher (Andou, Yukiko) with less pubs (412) fails most of the time. The top outputting researchers (Baba, Hideo @ 738, & Ogawa, Hisao @ 651) always fail to load. The strange thing is that I was having no problems like this up through early last week.

I'm using the 1GB instance size and have been trying to adjust the other settings to get it to work to no avail.

Below is a copy of the log after successfully loading data for a researcher named Abdullaeva, Zhypargul and then loading the data for Baba, Hideo where the app fails. Below that is the JS console from Firefox.

parts: Thank you for your reply, Andy.
your application is crashing because of out of memory conditions.

Good to know this for sure!

Before trying pagination, I decided to try the xml2 package instead of the XML package. While it has a much smaller memory footprint during file download, it doesn't seem to be as robust, and since I have never used it the notation is throwing me off a little.

Thanks again for your help.

-J
